goal: Go from zero ML knowledge to training and evaluating a small image classifier in PyTorch
interpretation: By the end, the learner understands supervised learning, gradient descent and backprop (with math), PyTorch tensors/autograd/training loops, how CNNs work, and can train and evaluate a CIFAR-10-style CNN while diagnosing overfitting. All of this is spread over four sittings of 90 minutes or less.
assumptions: Learner is fine with the CS229 lecture as a math-heavy start because they have calculus and linear algebra and asked for the math intuition.
Tensors and autograd are learned inside the StatQuest and CNN code-alongs. The pool has no standalone tensor-operations video in English.
The learner can do the Colab or local setup themselves.
feasibility_note: The goal is fully feasible. The candidate pool holds only about 5 hours of good material, so the plan uses far less than the 1200-minute budget rather than padding it.

sub_topics.why: Learn to detect overfitting with validation data and fix it with dropout and weight decay.

picks.title: Regularization in a Neural Network | Dealing with overfitting
picks.reason: Explains why overfitting happens and covers L1/L2 regularization, dropout, early stopping and data augmentation.

evidence.quote: Overfitting is when your model really closely fits the training data, so much so that it is not able to generalize really well to the real world.
Regularization is a way to limit this flexibility that the model has in hopes to avoid overfitting.
The idea behind L1 and L2 regularization is to adding the weights into the loss calculation or the cost function to punish the network for having higher weights.

picks.confidence_note: Concept only, but it pairs with the code-based video that follows.

picks.title: 13 PyTorch tutorial - Popular techniques to prevent the overfitting in a Neural Networks
picks.reason: Shows how to detect overfitting with a validation set and how to apply nn.Dropout and weight_decay in PyTorch, so the learner can fix an overfitting classifier. Sitting 4 totals about 80 min.

evidence.quote: The best way to tell if your model is overfitted is to use the validation data set during training
The most common regularization method is to add a penalty to the loss function in in proportion to the size of the weights in the model

picks.confidence_note: Practical PyTorch coverage of the regularization methods.

warnings: Only about 5.2 hours (about 313 min) of the 1200-minute budget is used. The candidate pool has no more good, non-duplicate English material, and I chose not to pad it.

Suggested sittings, each 90 minutes or less: (1) CS229 lecture; (2) codebasics GD, 3Blue1Brown ch.2–4, bias/variance; (3) StatQuest PyTorch, John Elder NN, codebasics CNN, Erai CNN; (4) NeuralNine CIFAR-10, AssemblyAI, datahacker.
No video covers PyTorch tensor operations or Dataset/DataLoader as a standalone topic. Learn them from the code-alongs and the official PyTorch docs.
No confusion-matrix or precision/recall coverage was found; evaluation here is accuracy and train-versus-validation comparison.

I kept NeuralNine over Patrick Loeber's CIFAR-10 CNN video because it spends more time on data loading, transforms and the test evaluation loop. I also dropped Aladdin Persson's MNIST CNN video as a near-duplicate that, by its own description, skips how convolutions work.
The codebasics CNN explainer uses TensorFlow for its other videos. I used only its conceptual explanation here.
